newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start slightly higher, Valeo falls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start slightly higher, Valeo falls.

text.p: French shares started slightly higher on Tuesday in cautious trade ahead of the U.S. presidential elections, dealers said.

Valeo dropped and CGIP jumped on news the holding company was buying a 20.2 percent stake in the car parts maker from Cerus, a French holding company controlled by Italian finacier Carlo de Benedetti.
CGIP had expressed its intention to buy the Cerus stake, ending a long stalemate as Cerus wanted to sell while big Valeo clients such as Peugeot did not want to see Valeo fall into foreign hands.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.68 points or 0.41 percent at 2,150.83 at 0915 GMT.
The CAC November future was up six points at 2,153.
CGIP, which on October 30 received 3.2 billion francs in cash for selling part of its stake in U.S. group Crown Cork and Seal, bought the stake at 330 francs per share.

"For CGIP it is a deal at a good price without any additional debts. For Valeo, it's the end of speculation (about another car parts group buying the Cerus stake and making a buy-out bid for the rest) and the share suffers from it," a dealer said.
